claims.text: MOA: primarily bacteriostatic; binds the 50S ribosomal subunit (inhibits protein synth).
claims.quote: Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic that is primarily bacteriostatic. It binds to the 50S subunit of the ribosome, thereby inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis.

claims.text: Treats: wide spectrum: gram (+) and gram (-) cocci and bacilli (incl anaerobes); Rickettsia, Mycoplasma, Chlamydia and Chlamydophila.
claims.quote: Chloramphenicol has a wide spectrum of activity against Gram-positive and gram-negative cocci and bacilli (including anaerobes) Rickettsia, Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, and Chlamydophila species

claims.text: Know: ⍉longer an abx of choice (bone marrow toxicity, alt, resistance), except serious multidrug-resistant infect still suscep to it and plague meningitis or endophthalmitis.
claims.quote: Because of bone marrow toxicity, the availability of alternative antibiotics, and the emergence of resistance, chloramphenicol is no longer an antibiotic of choice for any infection, except for Serious infections due to a few multidrug-resistant bacteria that remain susceptible to this antibiotic Plague meningitis or endophthalmitis

claims.text: Know: well absorbed PO; parenteral tx should be IV; distributes widely incl CSF; hepatic met, so it does ⍉accumulate in renal insuff.
claims.quote: Chloramphenicol is well absorbed orally. Parenteral therapy should be IV. Chloramphenicol is distributed widely in body fluids, including cerebrospinal fluid, and is excreted in urine. Because of hepatic metabolism, active chloramphenicol does not accumulate when renal insufficiency is present.

claims.text: CI: ↑rate of serious toxicities; contraindicated if another abx can be used instead.
claims.quote: Chloramphenicol has a high rate of serious toxicities and is contraindicated if another antibiotic can be used instead.

claims.text: Preg: assoc w gray baby syndrome in newborns (⍉teratogenic effects); may be used for RMSF if a second-line agent = required, but caution in the third trimester. Do ⍉use while breastfeed.
claims.quote: Use has been associated with gray baby syndrome in newborns but no teratogenic effects. It may be used in pregnancy to treat Rocky Mountain spotted fever if a second-line agent is required, but caution is warranted in the third trimester. Chloramphenicol enters breast milk. It should not be used during breastfeeding
claims.locator: Use of Chloramphenicol During Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

claims.text: Caution: bone marrow depression (most serious): reversible dose-related, or irreversible idiosyncratic aplastic anemia (< 1/25,000), which may develop after tx stops; do ⍉use topically.
claims.quote: Bone marrow depression (most serious) Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea Gray baby syndrome (in neonates) There are 2 types of bone marrow depression: Reversible dose-related interference with iron metabolism: This effect is most likely with high doses or prolonged treatment or in patients with a severe liver disorder. Irreversible idiosyncratic aplastic anemia: This anemia occurs in < 1/25,000 treated patients. It may not develop until after therapy is stopped. Chloramphenicol should not be used topically

claims.text: Caution: N/V/D; gray baby syndrome in neonates (hypothermia, cyanosis, flaccidity, circulatory collapse; often fatal); optic and periph neuritis w prolonged use.
claims.quote: Nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea Gray baby syndrome (in neonates) There are 2 types of bone marrow depression: Reversible dose-related interference with iron metabolism: This effect is most likely with high doses or prolonged treatment or in patients with a severe liver disorder. Irreversible idiosyncratic aplastic anemia: This anemia occurs in < 1/25,000 treated patients. It may not develop until after therapy is stopped. Chloramphenicol should not be used topically because small amounts may be absorbed and, rarely, cause aplastic anemia. Hypersensitivity reactions are uncommon. Optic and peripheral neuritis may occur with prolonged use. The neonatal gray baby syndrome, which involves hypothermia, cyanosis, flaccidity, and circulatory collapse, is often fatal.
